utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Judge Nosworthy will not be with us today or tomorrow. She is absent on other authorised Tribunal business. Yesterday at the end of the proceedings objection was taken to the use by Mr. Cepic of Exhibit P1100 on the basis that it had not been intimated as an exhibit to which reference would be made in the course of the cross-examination. The explanation for that is that it was misdescribed as P110. Mr. Lukic in supporting this objection by -- in his submission suggested that on occasions in the course of the evidence so far, similar objections to documents he intended to use had been sustained. In the Trial Chamber's researches since yesterday, we have been unable to identify any such occasion; on the other hand, there are examples at T 11275 and 18976 where objections of a similar nature were repelled, where in one instance the document had only recently arrived and in the other the Lukic Defence had not expected a development to occur -- a particular development to occur in the evidence. We are satisfied that in any event justice demands that we allow reference to this document, but it also does appear that the supporting argument advanced may have been wrong. Since this sort of situation may arise again, we would welcome the identification of any passages that may support the argument that was advanced by Mr. Lukic yesterday, because in another context it may be a more material point than we find it to be in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The cross-examination by Mr. Cepic will continue in a moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth continues to apply to your evidence today, as it did yesterday and on the first day. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We talked yesterday about documents about legal regulations, about the Law on Defence, about the Law on Internal Affairs. You mentioned at one point the Law on the VJ and the Rules of Service of the VJ. You will agree with me, won't you, that the Law on VJ and the Rules of Service of the VJ do not apply to the Ministry of the Interior, do they?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I apologise, but there are certain parts about graduates of secondary schools and the army and something about the MUP about the Law on the VJ, so there are certain parts that I believe to apply, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's try to be specific about this. You are one such case because you are a graduate of the military academy, and you were sent by the MUP for further education, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P985 brought up on our screens. This is the Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, before this shows up on our screens, you testified in chief about Article 17, a provision of Article 17 of that law.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Article 17, please. Could we have zoom in, please, the bottom of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, you were unable at one point in your testimony to provide a more specific interpretation about this part that reads: "Organs and units of the MUP."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how I came across, but I did do my best to explain that. I can repeat that, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, we've got that on the record already. Thank you. Do you agree that the legislator should have used this law to try to be more specific about what this expression means?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm no lawyer myself and it is not my place to go into the specifics of this law --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're quite right, Mr. Mijatovic. You'll move on to something else. That's a matter for us to deal with unless there's a particular difficulty as a matter of fact that you want to draw to our attention. The question of interpretation and how it might have approved is a matter we will deal with as a matter of law. But if you want to show -- if you want to point to evidence that there was a particular problem in fact caused by the terminology, then you can lead evidence about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will try to examine this witness in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, as a high-ranking MUP officer, will you agree with me that when MUP units are subordinated and there is the commander who commands over combat actions, the specific tasks of the engagement and assignments of the MUP units are not specified?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in an order regarding resubordination?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I did look at one of those. I don't think there are any specific tasks that are mentioned in those.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You agree that nothing is done by default when there is resubordination. There must be a specific order for it, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there must be an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are telling us that you saw an order on resubordination --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the answer of this -- this answer was wrongly entered in the transcript. If the question would be repeated and the answer as well, otherwise I would be leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's the question at line 15, Mr. Cepic. Would you ask it again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, I'm asking you, and you answered - there could be an error in the transcript - I'm repeating my question. Nothing is done by default when there is resubordination, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there is resubordination, it must be based on an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It comes to the same thing again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the other part of the question wasn't asked this time. "There must be a specific order ..." And the witness said something about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, twice he's said that there must be an order. What do you say was added to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I heard the witness saying there was an order, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mijatovic, did you actually say in response to that question the first time that there was an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I saw as I was being proofed two orders I think, one from the 3rd Army commander and one from the Pristina Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When did you first see these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, do you know whether the MUP staff in Pristina made any efforts or did anything for MUP forces to be resubordinated to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What sort of efforts do you have in mind? I know that in relation to 1999, or rather, 1998, both in 1999 and also when the air-strikes began the police units that were involved in anti-terrorist activity in the same way proceeded to work with VJ units, and as far as that was concerned there were no problems, as far as I remember. I did say yesterday, did I, because I think that was yesterday, wasn't it? I'm sorry about my pace. That the problem about resubordination, subordination, or as the law says, resubordination, was about all the other structures from the Ministry of the Interior. That's where problems arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know that that's an answer to the question, Mr. Mijatovic. I think it would be helpful to all of us if you were to address the particular question that was put just now which was: "Do you know whether the MUP staff in Pristina made any efforts or did anything for MUP forces to be resubordinated to the VJ?" The answer to that must be yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's difficult to provide a yes or no answer, Mr. President, because we're looking at units that were involved in combat actions and under the Law on Defence these are resubordinated. I don't think there was a problem with that, but there was a problem with the other thing, combatting crime, administrative affairs, that sort of thing. But the discussion was, as far as I remember, General Obrad Stevanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But I don't think we have seen any order where MUP were, in fact, resubordinated according to an order of -- within the Ministry of the Interior to the VJ, and that's what Mr. Cepic is asking you about, what efforts were actually made within your office to give effect to resubordination. And we understand the distinction between combat units or units being used in combat and the other operations of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I understand the question. I thought the previous one was in relation to an order down the army chain. I think Mr. Cepic asked me that question yesterday. I said that from the level of the ministry we received no order on resubordination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but his question is: What was done in the MUP staff to enable MUP forces to be resubordinated to the VJ? And he was referring to the MUP staff in Pristina, and that's the question, I have to say, I think you can answer either yes or no. Was anything done or was nothing done? The reason's another matter. The simple question at the moment is whether anything was done within the MUP staff in Pristina to give effect to resubordination of MUP forces to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The MUP staff could not take decisions like that. In Pristina there was also the assistant minister General Stevanovic. As far as I know he was in touch with people from the army and they discussed that; otherwise, the activities were proceeding the same as back in 1998. It's just that now the orders, "zapovesti," by the Pristina Corps now had the nature of an order with clear orders, or, "naradjenje," for police units -- my apologies, those involved in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, I find your evidence quite ambiguous and full of contradiction in some ways. You say one thing first and then another the next minute. Let's see what you can tell us about this. In May, at least as far as you know, what about the MUP's combat units, were they carrying out any tasks of the VJ in May?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very briefly, who seems to be attending this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant minister General Obrad Stevanovic, General Lukic, members of the staff, commanders of PJP detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: At number 1, that's you, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, members of the staff, I said so, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You personally attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I see, okay, and all these are members of combat units, the ones we see on the list, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are territorial detachments, there are two, as well as manoeuvre detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But they're all detachments, no SUP chiefs there, are there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 2 of this in the Serbian and page 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Dragan Nikolic, do you remember that person? Let's take him as an example, the 122nd Intervention Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name rings a bell but I can't remember the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It was a mechanised MUP brigade, right, the 122nd?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But it did have armour, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly the detachments had, but they did have some armour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: BJBAT, BOV 3?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is something that the mechanised brigade had and not the 122nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And which one was the mechanised one?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 124th.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Look at this, the 11th of May, deputy commander of the 122nd Intervention Brigade Lieutenant-Colonel Nikolic. Can you look at the last bullet point, please, and read it: "Relations with the VJ."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Relations with the VJ at the beginning was fraught with huge problems, and after clarifications, the situation improved and now cooperation is good."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Let's go to page 3 of the Serbian and page 7 of the English. Will you please look at item 6, Dragan Obradovic, the commander of the 86 Detachment of the PJP.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we zoom in, please, because I can't see this properly. Am I supposed to read this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the first and second bullet points, please. The second one is the one that matters. It starts: "The VJ ..."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We had no problems with the VJ, but neither do we have particularly good cooperation with them. We currently do not know where they are or what they're doing."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. What about the commander of the 85th Detachment, Major Rade Repic? This is page 4 in the Serbian or B/C/S and pages 9 and 10 in the English. Can you see that, sir? It's the third bullet point: "Cooperation with the VJ ..."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: "The commander of the 85th PJP Detachment, Major Rade Repic ..."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The cooperation with the VJ is good, although at the beginning there were attempts" -- there is something missing there, "but reason prevailed and now there is cooperation without any particular problems."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have page 15 in the English. The Serbian reference is 6, page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, who in the MUP was superior, personally superior, to these units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the PJP?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know - and I do know that - up until I think 1997 --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm talking about May 1999. Who from the MUP was the superior of the PJP unit?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just about to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please answer briefly.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with certainty because back in 1997 it was General Obrad Stevanovic. In 1997, he was appointed assistant minister and I don't know if he held on to his position as a commander of the PJP. He wasn't replaced by anyone at the time, so I can only assume that he continued in that position, but I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see his words in front of us on the record. Look at item 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in on item 4 in the Serbian. [In English] Could we have in English also, please, count 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please read it again, the first sentence of item 4, this has to do with General Obrad Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Stevanovic: Resubordination to VJ shall be in the spirit of cooperation and good exchange of information in the interest of the defence of the country and anti-terrorist struggle" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's quite sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the rest is important to with the proviso that we know who is cooperating --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If that's what counsel wants, that's what counsel gets. Mr. Lukic will be able to re-examine you, if he wishes to do so, in relation to that matter. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, you will agree with me that Mr. Obrad Stevanovic uses future tense, isn't that right? He says that it should be.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me about the date, is it 11th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the date, I'm asking you about the words.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Isn't he using future tense in terms of saying they should?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. That's not how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: They are using future tense.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not future tense. They are saying there needs to be, it's not future tense, at least in my interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So they are saying that something needs to be done, and it is not done; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that way. They are saying that they need to continue with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Very well. You're saying one thing and documents are saying something else, and this is not the first example of such behaviour, rather the sixth or seventh --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I kindly as the counsel to ask the question, not to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, sorry. Sorry, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask my colleague to ask the question, not to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I was about to do, to put a new question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, would you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That often is the case, Mr. Cepic, but we can do without the comments. It's really the second part of what you said in lines 17 and 18 that it's a matter for you to submit to us later. So let's stick to the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, item 5, just below this. Would you please read the first bullet point.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The police units are subordinated to the chief of SUP, heads of PJP, and heads of police have to attend every meeting of the SUP collegium."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this sentence clear to you, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this pertains --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see 5D1417, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, since we do not have the translation of this document, would you please read the title of this document, the heading.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Deployment of PJP in the region on the 17th of April, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you read 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "122nd Intervention Brigade," is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7th Company, Bradas, Bojcina, Kasindol, Krpne.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mijatovic, who is the commander of the 122nd Intervention Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we said earlier that it was Dragan Nikolic; however, whenever units are sent out, the commander is specified because people are sent out to rest and so on. So when a unit is established, the commander always needs to be designated, and I wouldn't be able to tell you at any point in time who was commander of what unit, company, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that Nikolic was deputy commander and that Colonel Dragan Zivaljevic was the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. As I have said to you, I can't remember the names because people rotated. If it were the same people all the time, I would have remembered their names, who were the commanders and so on, but people changed. Whenever a unit was deployed a commander was designated for that particular instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask you who made that designation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Senior staff -- senior officers in a detachment. When units are established by way of the decision of the minister, there was another document pertaining to establishment which specified how units were established. There was an establishment commander of a detachment. However, when a unit is sent out on a mission, it's not always the commander who is in charge of it because he has to rest as well. Therefore, instead of him, either his deputy or one of the lower-level company commanders headed the unit. It frequently happened that units were combined, which is to say that, for example, first three companies would be sent and then another three companies would be sent out to replace them. So the commanders were designated out of the entire command structure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, the 122nd Intervention Brigade, is that smaller than a detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there was a split there. The Belgrade detachment was split because they were active in two different locations and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's stop there. They're split in two or in more than two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think just in two. So a part of the 122nd remained --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now you've told us that the commander Nikolic might not be the commander when they're sent out on a particular occasion and that that commander might be changed. Who would make the decision whether to change Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decision would be made within that detachment, 122nd Detachment, they would be deciding who would go with the unit, not the staff. And I don't think the minister would do that either, because when the minister issues a decision, then in the decision it says that a unit needs to be sent, and they are the ones deciding the rest, people from the detachment and from the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So a detachment is sent out and it's left to the detachment to decide who will command them on this occasion; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. If the commander cannot go. Perhaps he was already there during a previous shift because people rotated every month or every 40 days. So the establishment commander had to have rest, and then they had to decide who would have the following shift, whether deputy commander, and if deputy commander was not available, then one of the company commanders. In the decision on sending out a detachment, it is not specified by names who would lead; no, that was normally decided at the level of a detachment. However, I do not exclude the possibility that in some of the decisions it was specified, but it wasn't the staff who did it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the detachment itself decides who will command it; is that what you're saying? It's yes or no. Don't go off on another tour of the country. Just tell me yes or no whether I've understood your correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, I didn't understand part of your answer, so would you please answer again. What is greater, a detachment or a brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to a military establishment --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, not the military. I'm asking you specifically with regard to the MUP of Serbia. There is mention of detachments and brigades. What is greater?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the military establishment, a brigade is larger; however, I don't know the exact numbers of the 122nd Brigade. It is possible that within the 22nd Detachment there was some additional people there, and the ministry was the one deciding upon it, and I wouldn't be able to tell you anything more about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was the 22nd Detachment within the composition of the 122nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat once again, 122nd Intervention Brigade, as far as I remember, was created by splitting the 22nd Detachment because they were active in two different locations, that was the need that existed most likely at the time. And just one figure was added, figure one, in order to see that they were part of the 22nd Detachment. This is why they were named 122nd. Now, as to the numbers, whether they received additional personnel because they needed them, I don't know. This was something that was decided at the level of the ministry, and I can't tell you anything about the numbers, who had more people, whether it was 122nd Brigade or the 22nd Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you testified, and on page 61 it was recorded that there was no reporting going on between the MUP staff and PJP detachments. Do you remember these words -- uttering these words?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that after anti-terrorist activities commanders of detachments did not submit reports, did not report the staff -- did not report to the staff; rather, they informed the relevant secretariats about certain events concerning which secretariats had to undertake certain measures or necessary measures. Now, as to whether they informed anybody in the course of combat activities, I wouldn't know that because I wasn't out on the ground, I wasn't following these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And similarly, the staff did not send to brigades or to detachments any orders in the course of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 5D1418. Could we see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, we don't have the English translation. Would you please read the heading of this document, but before you start doing that let me just put to you evidence of General Mandic, who claimed that in late May 122nd Intervention Brigade did not resubordinate itself to him for the purposes of carrying out a task. Did you know General Mandic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please read the heading of this document.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "MUP of the Republic of Serbia, staff of the MUP, dispatch number 139, 26th of May, 1999, Pristina" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To whom is it sent?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 122nd Intervention Brigade is sending this to Commander Zivaljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let's move on to the text.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Civilian persons to be returned to their villages. If that is not feasible, if that is not doable, we agree that they be deployed to positions you proposed. All persons fit for combat to be put in custody and turned over to the regional secretariat. In doing so, ensure that police acts in accordance with the law."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And signed by?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything that I can tell you about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just tell me, please, before you start reading this document, Lieutenant-Colonels Adamovic and Arsenijevic had both completed military academy, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In 1999 Arsenijevic was in charge of operations in the staff, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he replaced Adamovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. He was there dealing with operations?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you please read this heading.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "MUP of the Republic of Serbia, 122nd Intervention Brigade, communique number 09/99, 26th of May, 1999, Podujevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is sent to whom?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Chief of Staff of PJP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Will you please read what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there was no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. Read the text.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lines reached Bora 1 outside -- 88-88-78, rather 80-88-78; positions taken, 87, 86, 109, 110, 111, 98, 97, 95, and on from there. "We had several resistance points, the results so far are good, one slightly grey 0, collection points for refugees are at the following positions: 78 KA 90 and 111-90-91, among them about 150 fighters. Seek further instructions and location for refugee collection points, and I propose points 138 and 139. "Commander of the 122nd Intervention Brigade, Colonel Dragan Zivaljevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we please look at the upper right corner of this document, the handwritten portion, can the usher please move that slightly so we can see that. Thank you. In the upper right-hand corner, that's Lieutenant-Colonel Arsenijevic's signature, right, Mr. Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What does it say, the handwritten bit?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Lukic for familiarizing himself and taking a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is that underneath?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have one minute, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Mr. Mijatovic, you'll now be cross-examined by the Prosecutor, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mijatovic. Could you tell us when you first --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- joined the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I started working there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st of July, 1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And with regard to your work, what were you doing between 1992 and July of 1998 before you went to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1992, as far as I remember, I was working in a department, I was head of department within the police administration, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the whole time up until you went to Kosovo in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where were you located during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I went to Kosovo, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, between 1992 and July of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the ministry, in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When were you first promoted to the rank of colonel?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically whether it was in 1995 or 1996 when ranks were introduced in the police, and then we had certain terms that we had been using up to then, and then these positions were transformed into ranks in relation to all police members. And that was when my position at the time was transformed into the rank of colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And was that the rank you still held when you retired in 2004?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the exact date on which you were sent to Kosovo in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly, but I think it was in the first half of July, on or around the 15th, but while I was preparing for this testimony I was unable to track down the specific decision, and I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So there is a written document reflecting that, but you weren't able to find it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody who receives a mission like that gets a personalized decision. We talked the last time about me terminating work with the staff and being returned to one's original unit. The same applies to when one is sent out to work to be or attached to a staff, there is always a personalized decision on each of these appointments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we take it that the position you held before the ranks were introduced was at the same level as colonel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One could put it that way. I no longer remember exactly how positions were transformed into ranks, but I continued to do the same job within the police administration and the same applied to the previous situation where I held no rank, as to this new situation now that we suddenly had ranks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's the kind of document that would be in your personnel file, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, we've seen documents from the personnel file of David Gajic and Milorad Lukovic and Mr. Vilotic. You don't have your personnel file available?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not in my possession, but I think it should be in the ministry's -- the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who made the decision to send you to Kosovo in July 1998, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been either the minister or the chief of the public security sector, if you mean the decision on this appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So in terms of who signed the decision, it would have been either Minister Stojiljkovic or the Assistant Minister Djordjevic, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But do you know who -- who within the ministry made the initial proposal that you would be the person sent to Kosovo for that position of deputy head of staff, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who took that specific decision or who made that proposal, but that was what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before the written decision was issued, did anybody in the ministry come to you and say, Mr. Mijatovic, we're thinking of sending you to Kosovo? Or did you just get the document out of the blue?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told by General Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know if General Lukic had requested you personally?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, we see you described as the deputy head of staff. How many deputy heads of staff were there? Was there only one?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you were in that position from the beginning of -- from July 1998 until, what, the end of May 1999; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from July 1998 until the end of May 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Before I ask you questions about your testimony here, I'd like to just address a few items in your written statement. Do you have a hard copy of that, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The first one I want to ask you about is paragraph 13, and you're talking about some summaries that were made of the number of members of the police, et cetera, and a summary of the numerical strength and deployment of those in Kosovo. Did you work on that document? That this was being prepared in connection with the arrival of the OSCE-KVM mission.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is something that Dusko Adamovic did based on information that he had because he was in charge of keeping track the numerical strength of units. I'm sure I looked at it back then, and I think I forwarded this to KDOM, who at the beginning were in charge of the business of the Kosovo Verification Mission. I forwarded this to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at Exhibit P1224.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And with the usher's help I can hand you a hard copy, Colonel. I don't know if you've got it in your binder or not.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so -- probably it's there, but I can't quite ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Take a moment and tell me if you recognise that as something you'd seen before.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this table.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And with regard to the text, if you could look at -- I think it's on page 3 of the B/C/S and it's page 3 of the English, this is under item number 1 that's talking about protection of settlements and territory, right above item number 2. Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it makes reference that in the past period special police activities were directed at 19 municipalities with 306 settled areas and around 248.000 inhabitants. Do you have any disagreement with those numbers?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Affected by terrorist activity, so there's talk here of the 306 villages in 19 municipalities that were affected by terrorist activity. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware that those numbers were the same numbers that were presented to Mr. Milosevic and several other high-ranking politicians, police and military officials at a meeting of the body called the Inter-Departmental Staff for Suppressing Terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at this meeting myself, and I don't know what sort of information was shared. As I was being proofed for my evidence, I did look at this record, but I don't remember seeing these figures there. Maybe they were there, I just don't remember seeing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just take a quick look, if we may, then at Exhibit P2166. And, Colonel, this is the document that's described as the minutes of that meeting on the 29th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that's at page 5 of the English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I can give you a hard copy, Colonel, and I'll direct you to page 5 of the B/C/S where I've marked with a green marker this portion where it reports that: "The operations encompassed 19 municipalities and four towns ..." Do you find it? "And four towns with 248.239 residents or 15 per cent of the total 1.500.000 some residents in Kosovo and Metohija," do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, did General Lukic tell you about having attended this meeting in Belgrade on the 29th of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it in this record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, when did you see it in the record?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was being proofed for my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, but my question is: Did he tell you about it in 1998, around the time he went to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have. At the time it didn't matter that much to me and that's probably why I don't remember the date. I know he occasionally went to Belgrade, but I don't know exactly where to and what for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were General Lukic's number two man in the MUP staff in October 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And between July and the end of September 1998, you were aware that in Kosovo there was a plan for combatting terrorism that was carried out in several phases, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you looked at this document before during proofing, you will remember that the people attending included President Milosevic, President Milutinovic, Mr. Sainovic, the minister of the interior, the Chief of Staff of the army, the most high-ranking politicians and VJ and MUP personnel; and you're telling me that Mr. Lukic didn't tell you about this meeting? Is that your evidence under oath?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is this: He may have told me that he had been at that meeting, but I simply failed -- I had failed to remember before I looked at the document. It has been ten years, nearly ten years, so I really can't remember that; but the document shows that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go next to paragraph 16 of your statement, and in that one you're talking about how members of the KVM were informed about movements of the MUP or activity relating to the KLA. And that was part of your job in late 1998 and early 1999, wasn't it? You were on the commission?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was selected by the Ministry of the Interior to maintain links and contact with the leaders of the KVM in Pristina. At all levels there was a MUP officer appointed to be in charge of maintaining liaison with their centres from those that were at the municipal level to the HQ of the secretariat, not just me, all these liaison officers at the secretariats and municipalities, organizational units within municipalities maintained contact with the verification mission and they were under an obligation to report on matters such as these.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But am I wrong, weren't you pretty much the highest-ranking MUP member that was liaising with the KVM? I mean, other than General Lukic, in Kosovo weren't you the next highest guy?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was appointed for contact with the KVM. It wasn't General Lukic, it was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And there wasn't any higher-ranking MUP person involved in liaising with the KVM in Kosovo than you, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you were still in that position right up until the time they left, around the 20th of March or so, correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. You say in this paragraph 16 that during that time the police showed maximum restraint in taking any action against the KLA, except when it was attacked and had to respond in self-defence. Well, let me show you two VJ documents related to this issue and I'll ask you a couple of questions about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we first have P1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Colonel, I don't think you have this in your binder so I can give you a hard copy of it as well. Do you have the first one there, Colonel, it's dated the 12th of March, 1999, from the 549th Motorised Brigade? Do you see that one?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this regards the routing of the Siptar terrorist forces in Jeskovo village sector on 11 March 1999, in cooperation with the forces of the Prizren MUP.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You'll see --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- under item number 2 at the bottom of page 1 in the B/C/S, it is on page 2 of the English - do you see where it mentions the forces involved and it says: "MUP forces engaged were the 5th PJP Company of Prizren and the 37th PJP Detachment of Nis of a strength of about 300 men." Did you know about that action?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a local action in terms of its nature, the KVM, the liaison officer from the secretariat was supposed to inform their centre in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you'll see there were some 611 VJ men involved, so this action involving 911 VJ and MUP personnel, was that not something that was brought to your attention, as the number one MUP liaison? You didn't know about it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't remember in terms of specific locations, but there must have been reasons for it if the action had been carried out; and I'm sure that members of the verification mission were informed and told to follow because as I told you this was an action at a local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, and in your statement you told us that the police showed maximum restraint in taking any action against the KLA except when it was attacked. There's nothing in this document to indicate that the MUP was being attacked. This appears to be a planned operation that was carried out on the initiative of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now that nine or ten years have passed, I can't remember all of those details; but an action would not have been carried out without a reason. There must have been a reason, especially for the presence of the verification mission. So there must have been reasons, and the Prizren SUP, and most likely the army commander, were duty-bound to inform the KV centre in Prizren so that they could verify. Because it's impossible to inform about this and then carry out this action in a manner that is not obvious. This is not something that could have been concealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I take it from what you said, you didn't inform the KVM about this action involving 300 MUP personnel, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have said, this was a local action and KV knew about this action but was informed from the secretariat, from the Prizren secretariat, because that's where this was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what's your source of information for saying that KV knew about this action? By "KV," do you mean the Kosovo Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How do you know they knew about it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the responsibility of the secretariat to inform them. It was their responsibility to do so --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about whose responsibility it was. I'm asking you how you claim to know that they knew about it. Do you have a document reflecting that they were informed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have it on me, but secretariats were informing others about contacts with members of the mission. As for the specific developments, this was nine years ago, I can no longer remember, but they forwarded us information about contacts and developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And didn't you receive any daily information from the local MUP liaisons about what they were doing, or did you have no dealings with them?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We maintained contact through the secretariats. In principle this was the chief of the secretariat who was in charge of that, the chief of the OUP, or the commander of the police station, the highest-ranking police officers and those in the secretariat were in charge with maintaining contact with the KVM. We received regular daily reports from the secretariat, and I think as far as contacts were concerned with the KVM we had periodic information or periodic reports, and I believe this must be in one of those. But believe me, I really can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, would you agree with me that this is the kind of thing that you as a highest-ranking MUP liaison should have been informed about? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the reports were submitted. It's probably in one of those reports, but it was too long ago for me to remember and I don't have a document to jog my memory. It's probably in one of the documents, documents related to this trial, but I can't remember specifically. I'm not even sure I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So are you saying that the SUP in question was bound to submit a report to the MUP staff relating to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were bound to state in their daily report any developments relating to, as I said yesterday, because I see that certain units, especially units participated, if there were any developments that the secretariat had to do something about they would have had to put that in their report and then probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So is the answer: No, they were not bound to put it in their report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not submit detailed report about an action to the staff, just about possible events which took place during an action. So I'm sure that in some reports there was information, both concerning the KVM and the activities; but now that so much time has passed I just can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me approach it this way. If this took place and the fact that it had was concealed from you, would you be happy about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not claiming that it was concealed. I can't claim that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not my question. If it was concealed from you and did happen, would you have been happy about that? Would that have been acceptable to you in your position in the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They weren't supposed to conceal it. I don't see the reason for concealing it. It is impossible to conceal this because it is obvious that an activity is taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're just not going to answer my question? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I certainly want to answer, I'm just trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have the impression you don't want to answer my question because I've asked it twice, and I'll now ask it a third time. If this event took place and the information was kept from you - just accept that situation may have occurred - would you be -- would you find that acceptable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would not be acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why does it take --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It shouldn't take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, why does it take three attempts to get that answer from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I probably didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please bear in mind what was said to you yesterday about the way in which you consider and address the questions that are put to you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Lukic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Mijatovic tried to explain the way of information the flow of information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, sit down, please. Mr. Mijatovic can answer questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He did but you didn't recognise his answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you want to clarify that with him in re-examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- you will be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Second we have in the evidence that KVM was informed about this mission, it's 5D112 and 5D111 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- presenting the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just be quiet for a moment. Tell me where the question was answered, and I missed the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one moment. It's page 32, line 8, explaining the way of -- the way of information inside SUPs and MUPs, that it's not the way it works with the military, and he explained it yesterday, and he explained it the day before. And in the police case we have to start thinking in the police way, not to continue thinking in a military way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, as was often the case earlier in his evidence, he has told us that what has to be reported is developments that the secretariat had to do something about. They would have had to put that in their report. Now, that was not an answer to the question. The question could have been answered yes or no, and to clarify it, it was asked twice more before he gave a simple answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It depends. If there is something to be reported --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- then yes, if not, then no. So it can be yes and it can be no, depending on the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the question was: Are you saying the SUP in question was bound to submit a report to the MUP staff relating to this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and the answer to that must be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can be yes and can be no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, but if the answer is only if there are certain developments that need --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- attention -- now the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is no basic obligation to report this action is how that appears. We now have a different answer from --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a second. We now have a different answer from him, that there is an obligation to report. He has said at the very end of that the very opposite of what is in that answer as I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If somebody's killed, they have to report. If nobody's killed, they don't have to report. It depends on the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you want to take the solemn declaration now and give evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you confine yourself to making submissions on this in due course --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- and re-examining insofar as you think it appropriate to re-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is really going the wrong way because the Prosecution is not following this case. In this case this action has been reported in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not the issue that we are dealing with, Mr. Lukic. You do not seem to understand the point in issue, which is about the responsibilities of the various organs involved here to report to each other and let each other know the situation. Now, we're not -- I'm not suggesting to you that the routine in the police ought to be the same or was, in fact, the same as in the army. All I'm trying to do is discover what that routine actually was. Now, let us do that job and you can re-examine to your heart's content in due course if you feel it has not been properly explored. Mr. Hannis, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, if you could look at the second document, that's number -- that's our Exhibit Number P1999. That's a similar document from the 549th, this one dated the 18th of March regarding an action in the Kabas village sector on the 17th of March, where the Siptar terrorist forces were routed. And under item number 2 again you'll see the MUP forces engaged were the 5th PJP company of Prizren and the 37th PJP Detachment of Nis with about 350 men. And my first question to you about that is: Is there anything to indicate that the MUP was attacked and that's why they were responding in self-defence? Because as I read this report from Colonel Delic, this was an anti-terrorist action that was being carried out on the initiative of the VJ with the MUP. Do you have any information to the contrary?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Cepic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, this document that is being shown right now is the document of the Army of Yugoslavia not of the MUP of Serbia, and if I am wrong please correct me, but it is my impression that Mr. Hannis put the question as though this document was that of the MUP of Serbia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think he did do that. Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know that I did. It certainly seems to speak from itself as the 549th, Colonel Delic, we all know he was with the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, did you have some kind of information that shortly prior to the 17th of March, 1999, the MUP was being attacked by the terrorists in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't now pin-point where this location is, and I really can't remember. It's been a long time and there were many locations where they attacked, and I really can't remember whether this was reported and it should have been, that there were attacks, that they were attacking civilians, that there were victims and so on; but I really couldn't tell you anything more about the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 20 of your statement and you're continuing to talk about KVM. You say: "They were constantly trying to prevent the police from performing their tasks. They thus declared a patrol which was carrying out regular patrol duties to be a 'mobile check-point' and a patrol which had halted a 'position' accusing us of violating the agreement in this way."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have a look at Exhibit 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I've got a question about this issue for you, and if I could have the assistance of the usher I'll give you a hard copy of P1991. If I could get those other documents back from you. And if you look at the first page, this is a record from the meeting of the ministry staff with the minister of the interior, of the chiefs of the SUPs, the commanders of the PJP on 21 December 1998. And you're listed as being at that meeting. You recall this one, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see, based on the minutes, that I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have any independent recollection of this meeting, other than seeing your name on the minutes?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember these meetings, but not the details of them. If I'm listed on the list, that means that I did attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you could go to page 4 in the B/C/S, and in English we're at page 7. We'll see that you're speaking. You apparently addressed the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you mention that there were certain omissions regarding reporting, and you talk about the 27 observation points or posts that we understand were allowed under the agreement. And just a little further down you say: "You should not use the term 'mobile check-points' in reports because they don't exist, but rather use police patrol." So the problem was those guys out in the field doing this work were reporting themselves as mobile check-points and that was causing you problems with the KVM, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that this term was coined by the representatives of KVM because they kept saying that they shouldn't organize mobile check-points and so on, and I think that's where the mistake is because in our plans and in the plans of police station we do not have such term, mobile check-points, we just have a term patrol; and this term here is a wrong one and they used it, and that is why attention was drawn to this fact. I have never heard of a mobile police check-point ever since I came to work in the police force until that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you saying that MUP members who were reporting were not using the term mobile check-points before this meeting in December 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely. This is why a warning ensued for this term not to be used because it doesn't exist in police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, can you find a point to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a good point for me to take the break, Your Honour. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We have to have a break again, Mr. Mijatovic, so could you leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll resume shortly after five past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is coming in, can I make an oral application to have the updated translation of Exhibit P2805 substituted into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is P2805?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: An issue arose regarding the translation the other day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is the minutes of the MUP staff meeting in Pristina on 5 November 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has the updated translation been exhibited to all parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm informed that it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there any objection to that course of action? Does anyone need more time to consider it? Very well. We shall authorise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, we were looking at Exhibit P1991, which is that meeting on the 21st of December, 1998, that we just talked about mobile check-points. If you could continue to the end of your remarks, I think it's still -- or I think it's actually on perhaps B/C/S page 5, and I know it's on page 8 of the English. The last thing that you spoke about to the group was you said: "After bringing anyone into a police station, physical force must not be used and people must not be beaten or have injuries inflicted on them." Why was it necessary to bring that to the group's attention on the 21st of December, 1998? Had that been a problem before this day?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that it was a problem in terms of happening frequently, but if this needed to be drawn attention to then it means there must have been a case where this happened. I claim with full responsibility that action was taken against people who did this, and I'm saying this, that measures need to be taken to ensure that this doesn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My next question regarding your statement is paragraph 24, again talking about KVM. You say: "When asked why they had not immediately reported what had happened to the nearest police station or liaison officer and established the facts with them, as a rule they did not have any answer. In the same way, they reported seeing police vehicles painted like theirs with KVM markings, which is a blatant lie." Now, in your earlier testimony you told us I think on more than one occasion that you were not in the field. So how do you know it was a lie regarding their reported sighting of police vehicles painted with KVM markings? You weren't out there to observe that, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there out on the field and see vehicles. No, they reported that and we asked that additional details be given to us, based on which we could conduct a check, we could verify this. We knew neither the make or license plate of the vehicle or anything else that would indicate it was a police vehicle. So I don't know based on what they concluded that this was a police vehicle when they didn't have any supporting data. This is why I drew this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to paragraph 31 and 32 of your statement. You talk about how after the time or during the time KVM spent in Kosovo, the KLA strengthened its organization and consolidated itself. In paragraph 32, you mention how members of the MUP had to put up with all of this including the murder and wounding of their colleagues out of respect for the agreement. On the other hand, the KLA did not accept any obligations. You know, don't you, Colonel, that the KLA didn't sign the agreement. They were not parties to this agreement between Yugoslavia and the OSCE; you know that, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that and that's precisely where the problem lies. Because had they been a signatory then they would not have been allowed to take up positions and block the roads that used to be controlled by security forces or police. This is why I said this, that they had no obligations according to the agreement and this is why they acted the way they acted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree with you that that's probably a big part of the problem, but your statement says the KLA did not accept any obligations. They didn't have any obligations under the agreement, did they; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's true that they didn't have any obligations, and this is why I say that they acted in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I ask you for a yes or no answer, all I need is yes or no. Do you understand that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm afraid that this is once again an ambiguous question, and if I were to give a yes or no answer then it would be wrong. That's why I'm trying to be clear so that my answer is not taken as a wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was an ambiguous question? The one I just asked you about whether you understood when I say, Yes or no, I just need yes or no. Is that what you're calling an ambiguous question, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is a matter of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Speaking for myself, Mr. Hannis, it is important to observe that in paragraph 32 it doesn't say "did not accept any obligations under the agreement," they just didn't accept any obligations which is rather a different matter. But you are quite right that the simple question that you put about whether they had any obligations under the agreement is one that can be answered yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the paragraph is not in any way misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the -- Your Honour, I think if I may, the sentence immediately prior to the one about the KLA was the members of the MUP had to put up with this out of respect for the agreement, and I guess that's how I read "agreement" into the second sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But I take your point and I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, paragraph 39 of your statement refers to a Pristina Corps command document Exhibit P1434, and you mention the fact that there is a reference to MUP forces command and you say at the very end of that paragraph: "This document was certainly not written in the police." Did anybody suggest to you that it was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't suggest to me that it was so, but in our police jargon we do not use such a term as command of MUP forces because such a term does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you read the whole document or just that first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this order?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, that whole --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I definitely read the heading and this part, but this is erroneous terminology. We do not use such terminology. This is why I said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll hand you a hard copy of the whole order. This is P1434, and this is dated the 19th of September, 1998, from the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say in your statement that this document was written by someone who understands neither the structure nor the work of the police. Would you look at item 5.1, it's under task. I'm not sure which page it is in B/C/S, I don't have it in front of me. It's page 7 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
