utterances.text: Thank you. And the task for Battle Group 125-1 is to support attack by the 3rd Detachment of the PJP, the JSO, and the Pec PJP Company. And if you'll go on through, you'll see other tasks for other VJ groups supporting specific MUP units, PJP detachments, PJP companies, the SAJ, so would you agree with me whoever wrote this did know apparently something about the units of the MUP that could be involved in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this does not include SAJ, it involves JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, it does involve JSO, but I think you'll find a reference to SAJ further on if you continue. Did you come across it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 5.2, the second one talks about engaging Battle Group 15-2 to support attack by the 8th PJP Detachment, the Djakovica PJP Company, and the SAJ. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's towards the bottom. I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you next about paragraph 40 in your statement, Exhibit P3049, and this is an order that is entitled: "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija." I'll trade you documents now, if I may. You say in your statement that you recognise this document as belonging to the Pristina Corps. Can you explain for us how you know that. There does not appear to be a reference to the Pristina Corps in either the heading or the signature block.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, two things. The first one is that it says here military secret on the document. As far as I know, it only exists within the Army of Yugoslavia, a military secret. Perhaps I'm wrong, but I think that that's how it is. On the other hand, looking at the text of this order I can see that it doesn't differ from the text in the previous order that we have analysed in terms of terminology used and content of the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And as I understand your testimony, you had not seen any orders with Joint Command on them prior to coming here to prepare to testify in this case, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: During your proofing did you see one of the document --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I apologise. I apologise. I didn't see the document before the proofing. I saw the document for the first time during the proofing. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I understood. And during your proofing did you see a Joint Command document with Joint Command in the heading but actually signed by General Lazarevic? Did you see that one? We have one in evidence, it's Exhibit P1967. Do you recall seeing that one?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the proofing?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: During the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Have I seen any other document with this heading and signed by General Lazarevic; is that what you're asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's my question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing a document signed by General Lazarevic, but I did see some other orders with the heading saying Joint Command, but I don't remember seeing them with the signature of General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, there's a noise in my -- there's noise in my headphones --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you Exhibit 6D798?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear anything due to the noise. It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is it okay now?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now one that I think you saw the other day, it's Exhibit 6D798 -- or actually this is a short one. We'll look at it in the screen. The minutes of a meeting on the 22nd of July, 1998, at the Pristina MUP. Do you recall this one?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've seen this during the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, and I think during your testimony the other day it was brought to your attention. This was the one where there was a discussion of -- well, on the agenda there is mention of item number 3, defining tasks in the implementation of the global plan. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And listed among the attendees are General Djordjevic and Stevanovic, Lukic, yourself, all the chiefs of the SUP and all the commanders of the PJP. Could you look at the second page of your document because what we have -- we have a report from three of the SUP chiefs and then the document suddenly ends. This does not appear to be a complete document to me, does it to you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Because we've seen some of these other meetings and usually all the chiefs speak and oftentimes at the end of the minutes there is a notation of the time that the meeting ended and either it's signed staff or signed by an individual on the staff as the note-taker. Do you know where the rest of the minutes for this meeting might be?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you shown this document during your proofing?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did -- I was shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did it strike you at the time that there was something missing from it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall at the time on the 22nd of July what you knew about this so-called global plan? Had it been discussed with you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I heard this from the general that a plan had been adopted and that pursuant to that plan there was to be anti-terrorist activity. No one from the ministry had been involved in drafting the plan. I said that several days ago, and that's why there was a bit of a problem with the forces that were supposed to be involved in this anti-terrorist activity because a far greater scale of force had been envisaged than the sort of force that was available to the MUP at the time in terms of how dangerous and risky this sort of war was likely to prove. So yes, I had heard about the plan before this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, you told us about that yesterday I think or the day before, that -- the concerns about the number of men that were going to be required. It seems to me that that was something that was probably discussed by General Lukic or General Stevanovic or General Djordjevic at that meeting. Do you recall them talking about it during the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they talked about it during the meeting, but I know they were worried about how this whole thing would be carried out since they knew that they were facing a shortage of manpower. You must understand, it's difficult for me to think back ten years like that and remember exactly who said what. It's possible that the officers said at that meeting that we are facing that type of a problem it's just that I can't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And are you aware that on that same date apparently between the hours of 1900 and 2330, General Lukic was attending a meeting of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that General Lukic was attending some meetings in the evening. I heard at the time, I don't know when exactly -- there's this term, Joint Command, which was a recurring term, but believe me I don't know when I first learned about that or who told me. But as I've been saying over the last few days, I never came face-to-face with this command. I never got to know what it really meant, and that's why I never interpreted those meetings to be meetings of the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And if I tell you in those minutes at page 3 of the English General Lukic is recorded as having said on the 22nd of July: "A meeting was held with all the platoon commanders and then with the MUP chiefs ..." That's a meeting that's reflected in that exhibit you have in front of you, isn't it, on the 22nd of July, where the global plan is on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Leaving aside the issue of the fact where we still seem to be talking about minutes, whereas we shouldn't be, then at least the witness should be shown exactly what my learned friend the Prosecutor is telling him about. This is some sort of semi-document that we see on the screen in front of him and the question being asked is different altogether. I think the witness should be given a chance to see for himself whether that is the thing or not. Can I have instructions from the Chamber, please, should I stop mentioning this thing about minutes and records and notes whatever and then Mr. Hannis can just fire away any which way he likes? I think I'm beginning to boring myself slightly already, let alone how much I must be boring the Chamber to death with this objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are two points in that submission, Mr. Fila. One is the general question of the name or description of the document, and I think we've dealt with that already and made it clear to you that the fact that it's called minutes won't really weigh. So on that point, yes, you can rest easy that you do not need to constantly remind us of that obligation. So far as the second point is concerned, which is in the -- in this circumstance is it necessary to let the witness see the document, well we don't think it is in this case, but obviously if that issue arises again that's one you do have to draw to our attention. But where it's a meeting that the witness did not himself attend, then it's sufficient if Mr. Hannis quotes accurately from the record of the meeting and then says to the witness: Does that not sound like a description of the meeting you were at, and that's the question he's asking. So can we proceed on that basis, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Don't feel bored any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The notes of the 22nd of July, 1998, meeting of the Joint Command has General Lukic noted as saying, among other things: "A meeting was held with all the platoon commanders and then with MUP chiefs ..." That sounds like a description of the meeting in that exhibit in front of you, 6D798, because that was with those people on the 22nd of July, 1998. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same day, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I know that, but would you agree with me that that's probably the same meeting he's talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document we are talking about, this was in the evening and you said this was done during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the evening he's talking about having had a meeting with the MUP chiefs and the platoon commanders; isn't that the meeting that's in the document in front of you. That was held on the 22nd of July, I assume sometime before 7.00 at night, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do apologise. I failed to understand the first time around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm finished with your statement. Let me ask you about some of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on there, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one thing. You did say a short time ago, Mr. Mijatovic, that you had heard the expression Joint Command at the time, but you couldn't recollect the source of the information. What are the possibilities? From whom could you possibly have heard of the Joint Command at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say for sure. I really can't say for sure. I don't know who took the minutes from these meetings. I cannot really identify the handwriting. There are minutes from a meeting that I attended, I looked at others too. I can't tell despite this, and I see whoever was in charge would put the header there, Joint Command. I can only make assumptions about this, but I can't remember precisely who it was. I can't point my finger at a person and say that was him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This next comment is simply an indication -- a statement of the obvious, it doesn't suggest any conclusion whatsoever. But one obvious possibility is General Lukic because you're in regular contact with him and there are suggestions in this case that he went to meetings which could be connected with this concept of the Joint Command. Now, who else might fall into that category apart from him? And by that I mean people that you would be in touch with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be quite frank, I don't remember General Lukic ever told me that he was off to a meeting of the Joint Command, but I did see people from the military every now and then and someone may have used the term, the simple reason being we carried out those actions together. And I think I said yesterday the military terminology is what it is, they call everything a command. For example, this document a while ago, the MUP force command, I think there was a reference to that. So the ministry staff was sometimes referred to as a command, it was a matter of terminology for them. I think it's possible that precisely on account of this cooperation that we had on anti-terrorist activity they made this link between the Pristina Corps command and instead of the staff of the MUP a Joint Command and then like that one thing leads to another. And in that context perhaps I might have heard someone in a conversation refer to, this is a Joint Command, but then again I have to point out the following: I never learned of the existence of this body and there was nothing to indicate that such a body existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who was your closest or most frequent contact in the military?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1998 I used to see General Pavkovic, I used to see Djakovic, I had a schoolmate from the academy, my time at the academy, who was also a corps commander, unfortunately his name escapes me right now, I think he was a signalsman, and some other officers too. I can't remember all of them right now. I think there was a man named Colonel Starcevic, and then before him there was Bojevic, but that was earlier on. I used to know him because his brother was a professor of mine back at the academy. It was like that, there was several people that I would come across.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, I would now like to ask you a few questions about Exhibit P1505. This is a document you looked at when you were testifying before. This is that 16th June 1998 decision of the minister of the interior establishing a staff for the MUP in Kosovo and Metohija. Do you have a copy of that or do you -- are you okay to work off the screen?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have it in the binder, but it's a short document so I think the screen will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. One of the questions that you were asked about was whether or not the head of the staff could affect any decision about the members of the staff, and at page 22165 in our transcript you said: "No, no influence whatsoever because the decisions on sending people there were made either by the minister or heads of various sectors." I'm not sure where you'll find it on the B/C/S, but it's on page 1 of the English, and it's right before item number 2. I think you'll have to go to page 2 of the B/C/S. You will recall we talked a little bit -- I think Judge Bonomy asked you about the section that talked about the expanded staff shall also include chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs and centres and branches of the RDB, but the next sentence you'll see it says: "Other members of the ministry may be appointed to the staff on request of the head of the staff." Doesn't that indicate that General Lukic as head of the staff could have some influence on the make-up of the staff because he could make requests about personnel under this decision? Isn't that what that means?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we spoke about that. Was he in a position to affect a decision. The decision would have been taken by the minister or whoever the minister authorised to take that decision. Certainly, though I don't think this would have been in anybody's way, anybody can make a request or a proposal but not everybody can take a decision, that's one thing. Secondly, was he consulted in relation to anyone in particular because, for example, the request might turn out to be this, to send a man down the line of criminality.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is a direct quote from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But not in terms of the concrete personality because that was my understanding of the question. Because requests and proposals are not decisions, they're not part of a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, pursuant to the decision, the only person listed as being able to make a request is the head of the staff, right? That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On behalf of the staff, yes. At staff meetings, within the staff, there would be a problem that would show up and then it would turn out that somebody else would have to be sent and then there's a request, I need a man like this or that, send someone, they decide who to send, they take a decision, and they send him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where you get on behalf of the staff. It just says: "Other members of the ministry may be appointed to the staff on request of the head of the staff." Doesn't that mean that General Lukic, for whatever reason, whether it's on behalf of the head of the staff or whether it's just because he wants somebody, he is the one who can make the request, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says here that he can make a request. It doesn't mean that it will be granted, but requests can be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It also doesn't explicitly say that he can request particular people. It's a question of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And does it mean that he can ask to have the current people replaced? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked for -- to be replaced and I talked about my previous testimony, the three members of the staff who were injured and the assessment was they should be sent back home and that other people should be appointed. I can't remember whether that was dealt with on the phone or whether there was a document or something. Anyway, these three people over there should have been known that these three people were to be replaced, and sure enough General Lukic must have requested that someone else be sent out in their stead. And that's precisely what was done, Arsenijevic, Petar Bogdanovic, and Joca Gucic came instead of the three who were sent back.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yesterday you went through the -- yesterday or the day before you went through this list Exhibit P1505, and I think there are 13 names on that list. You named ten people who you said were on the staff, this is at page 22167, and of the ones that you named six of them, by my count, are on the list in P1505, that is General Lukic and then six others, Goran Radosavljevic, Novica Zdravkovic, Radovan Vucurevic, I think Rajcic, Krdzic --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krdzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Krdzic --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Cankovic, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And Milan Cankovic, correct. So are you saying those other six somehow between the 16th of June, 1998, and early July, the first half of July when you arrived, they had been -- those other six had been removed from the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I didn't know whether they, as they were in the decision, but did they over that month - my apologies, I have some throat problems. I don't know if at all during that month before my arrival they had been doing anything at the staff or not. I hadn't hear that they had been doing anything, and when I came there, I didn't find them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Any time you need a break because of your throat, let us know.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just apologising because I do have problems every now and again so I have to cough, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If they -- I take it that if they had been removed from the staff there would be some sort of document reflecting that, wouldn't there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There is simply no document showing that I was member of the staff, Adamovic, Slovic as far as I remember. I never saw a document like that, not that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The document appointing you did not reflect that you were to be a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that. The decision on the establishment of the staff with a list of its members doesn't exist. On the 16th of June the last decision was adopted, and I myself arrived in July, after that decision had been passed. Therefore, you won't find my name in any of those decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, but I guess --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I really can't say why.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess I'm confused about the document that sent you to Kosovo. Did that say that you were going to Kosovo to be the deputy head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday or possibly two days ago I was talking about that. The decision on that appointment must have existed. I don't own a copy, I don't have one at all, I don't know where it is. As I was being proofed, I didn't come across this among the documents; therefore, I can't say what exactly it says. But I'm positive that the decision can be found somewhere in my file, the file with my name on it in the Ministry of the Interior. So the decision on the appointment is there but there is no decision on the establishment of the staff, such as the one on the 16th of June, 1998, with a list of the people who actually made up the staff. I didn't see a decision like that, with Adamovic, Slovic, and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But that is how it should have worked, right? Should there not have been a written document reflecting that you, Adamovic, Slovic, and was the other one Arsenijevic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arsenijevic came later, he came in 1999. Adamovic, Slovic, and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But is it the way it worked that there would have been a document appointing each of those individuals to the staff, or do you know how it worked?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I didn't see that kind of decision. Means it not there. Should this have been the case? Not my call. This is something for the top level of the ministry, the minister, or one of the heads of sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So you're the deputy head of staff. How do you know who the other staff members are? Does one of these guys walk in the room and say, Hi, I'm one of the new guys on the staff or didn't you receive some kind of document reflecting that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think already that's not like that. We had our rooms, we had a schedule, you knew who was working in which room. I saw those people on a daily basis, and I knew that they were staff members. That's all I can say, but I don't have a document showing that; that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And did you not have during your time there as deputy head of the staff any kind of organizational chart that you kept in your office showing who was on the staff and what their various positions and responsibilities were? You must have had a phone list or something, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew who the staff members were. That we have all the phone numbers for everyone, maybe there was some sort of a directory being used at the time, it's just that I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: I should intervene here to just help you in recalling that when you leave a position and you go to another position there's a movement order, and that movement order you have then to show to people from whom you will get the salary. But things cannot be done just verbally because you have to draw a salary, you have to take a position. Now, think of that, wouldn't there be a written order, and didn't you get one and how would there be a movement without a written order? How would you know where you were going and the other people who were your recipients, how would they know that you have come and joined? It's leaving a charge, what they call relinquishing a charge and taking over a charge. I mean, this is what usually happens. I don't know, it may be strange here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, again I have this impression that we are talking at cross-purposes. It's a shame that we're not speaking the same language. I'm sure it would be much easier for us to understand each other. I was saying that we all had personalized decisions on our appointments to the staff. So that's one part of the business. Each and every one of us who were sent to the staff in Kosovo and Metohija would get a personalized decision. Miroslav Mijatovic is hereby being appointed to the staff, day being such and such, and that was the decision that we followed. Mr. Prosecutor, as far as I understand the question, is asking me this, he's asking me about the format of this decision to establish this staff such as the one dated the 16th of June, 1998, which states precisely who the leader of the staff was, who the assistant was, and all the names you can find there. Right. We arrived there and those people weren't at the staff, such as Lukovic, Trajkovic, and I can't remember all of them right now, David Gajic. So this means they weren't functioning at the staff at the time we arrived. I'm not sure if I'm coming across. It's true we are not on that list, that decision, on the establishment of the staff. It's not us, it's them who is on the list, but it wasn't them who were there. It was us, and we were doing the work. That's why I said the other day. If you accept the fact that the members of the staff were Gajic, Lukovic and Trajkovic because that's what the decision states and then on the other hand, Mijatovic, Adamovic, and Slovic were not members of the staff and then you accept that and, in fact, they were, and then at the same time you have two untruths which you take to be the truth. I'm not sure if I'm coming across with any degree of clarity at all but that is certainly is my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Later on, though, in 1999 there were replacements including the appointment of Arsenijevic, and Mr. Hannis is anxious to know how you would know that they had actually been appointed to the positions that they then occupied.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He had a personalized decision on this appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So nothing would be sent to you in writing confirming his appointment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, apart from the decision itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see that sort of a document, as far as the staff was concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you and Adamovic and the others whose names don't appear on this list arrive all at the same time, you, Adamovic, Slovic, or did you come at different dates?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we arrived -- no, I came separately as far as I can remember. Adamovic was already down there. Slovic, I think that he arrived a bit later, but to tell you the truth I don't know. It was all at about the same time. I just don't remember any more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a hypothetical question. Say I'm the minister who issued this decision or I'm his Chief of Staff and some problem comes up where I need to get ahold of the assistant head for analysis, who on this list is Rasko Milenkovic. Now, from what you tell me he was not on the staff when you arrived in July of 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that he was there for a couple of days. I can't put a face to the name. The name seems familiar, but I can't remember the face --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and that's why I can't be certain whether Slovic arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. How about Milorad Lukovic then, you told us he was not on the staff, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't. He was there on the list just as Lukovic and Trajkovic, but he didn't perform any tasks at the staff while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, he may have not performed any tasks, but does that preclude him from being a member of the staff. He may be on the staff to receive information or convey information, but he might not have any tasks. Isn't that possible?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He didn't sit in the premises used by the staff at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. So if I'm the minister or the deputy or the Chief of Staff and I'm trying to get ahold of the assistant head of staff for special operations in Pristina MUP staff, I'm going to rely on this list, aren't I? How am I going to know who's holding that job if you tell me this list was incorrect. Was the ministry notified in some way when all these changes were made?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody else could have produced those changes except for the minister, and it's obvious that he did not issue the second decision of the similar content listing Adamovic, myself, and Slovic as replacements for some of the other people. So it was a problem that minister didn't do it, but I can't really comment on it. I don't know why he didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, related to that then let's take a look at Exhibit P1811. With the usher's help, I'll give you a hard copy of this one. And before you go away from P1505, will you note the number on that is DT01 number 1580/98, you agree with me, in the upper left corner of the front page, that's the registry number on that document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the previous document, I don't have it on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'll show it to you if you need to, but I'll ask you to take my word for it and trust that somebody on the otherwise would jump up if I was incorrect. Do you see this one from 31 May 1999, this is a decision --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I didn't even hear what you said. I wanted to see what you said, but I didn't really follow. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The document you were just looking at previously, the 16th of June, 1998, has a registry number of DT01 number 1580/98, but right now we're looking at the 31 May 1999 decision by Minister Stojiljkovic establishing a MUP staff for the suppression of terrorism. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That was the first time you ever saw it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you'll go to the -- and it names General Lukic and the other members and, as you know, you're not -- your name is not listed on this one. But if you go to the last page, item number 6 says this decision shall enter into force on the 1st of June, 1999, and then it goes on to say: "This decision supersedes the decision on the establishment of the ministry's staff for the suppression of terrorism, DT01 number 1580/98 of 16 June 1998." Reading that it seems to me that the ministry didn't find any need to enter a decision changing the staff that it had established on 16 June 1998, right? There's no intervening document. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I understood this sufficiently because the decision on the 31st of May was automatically superseded by the decision on the 16th of June, and I did not know whether the minister had to inform somebody specifically about this. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Maybe there's a translation problem, but it was the decision of the 16th of June, 1998, that was superseded by this decision of the 31st of May, 1999, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's what it says there in the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the reason I'm asking a question is an outsider who's not familiar with how the MUP works and the rules of administration and personnel are, et cetera. It looks like there was nothing from the minister's level about a change in the make-up of the staff between June 16th, 1998, and May 31st, 1999, because surely that would have been mentioned in this document and those other changes would have been superseded as well, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you're right. Given that we were at the staff, this decision of the 16th of June should have been amended in order to include us who were not there, and then that would have been superseded by the decision on the 31st of May but that wasn't done. And such a decision never was issued, and I don't know why not. And had it existed then the decision on the 31st of May would have listed that it was superseding this intermediary decision, based on which we can see there are these two decisions, the one from June 1998 and May 1999 and no one in between. This is my interpretation, and I really can't explain this any better.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The MUP staff for Pristina, you and General Lukic and all the others you have told us about, where were you physically located in Pristina from July 1998 through May of 1999 -- well, let's go between July 1998 and the beginning of the war, 24th of March, 1999, where were you physically located?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Physically we were located in Pristina, in the building of the secretariat of the interior of Pristina. I can't remember how many storeys there are in that building, but as far as I can remember we were on the third floor of one of that wings of that body -- building where we had six or seven offices, and we were there throughout the time until the beginning of the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And so you were in the same building as the Pristina SUP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We've heard that Mr. Joksic and Mr. Gajic, David Gajic, and later on Mr. Vilotic were members of the RDB. Were they housed in the same building with you between July 1998 and March 24th, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that they are members of the state security sector and that they were located in a separate building which was very close. It was a building right next to the secretariat, but it was a separate building. State security centre from Pristina was based in that building, and just as we were a staff in the building of the Pristina SUP, they, since they had been sent from Belgrade, were using the premises of their organizational unit in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And after the MUP/SUP building in Pristina was bombed, where were you located for the duration of the war? And when I say "you," I mean the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understood the question. We changed our offices frequently because this situation was such that bombing was taking place daily and for our safety we had to frequently change our locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Joksic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please speak into the microphone, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Joksic told us that during the war he was with General Lukic, I think almost every day - I'm trying to find the exact quote - at page 22006, line 14 he said: "I spent the entire war virtually together with General Lukic." Is that correct? Was he and anyone else from the DB --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Joksic was frequently there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to Zivko Trajkovic, you said: Although he was listed as a member, you say he wasn't. When you came down there you didn't find him. You saw him at two or three meetings. But then you say, so he was not a member of the staff. How do you come to that conclusion? How do you know he was not a member of the staff? He's on the list in that 16 June document. You say he came to two or three meetings in the premises. Why do you say he was not a member?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that he wasn't a member because I didn't see him daily, like other staff members in the premises of the staff. He didn't have his office at the staff. He didn't perform any tasks within the staff, that is to say he was physically not present in the premises of the staff except when meetings were held in the premises of the SUP Pristina, that is to say where the staff was. Meetings with the senior officers of the police from Kosovo and Metohija, including heads of secretariats and units that had been dispatched there. Zivko Trajkovic throughout that time was in the unit which he led, and that was a special anti-terrorist unit of the ministry from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the main reason why I said this -- in fact, it's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You say it's a fact because you say so? Is that stated in your rules of how the Ministry of the Interior works or in the administrative rules? Where does it say that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is not written anywhere. It's a fact that that's how it was, that was the factual situation. He wasn't present in the premises of the staff. He did not perform any tasks at the staff, he did not have an office there. He was in his unit. That was the actual state of affairs. It is also a fact that his name is listed down as a member of the staff in the decision. I'm not denying that, but I'm saying that factually he wasn't a member of the staff, he wasn't there, and formally he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You recall, I think it was Judge Bonomy who asked you about this previously, that in this decision of the 16th of June, 1998, where it talks about the staff it says: "The expanded staff shall also include chiefs of the secretariats for internal affairs, centres and branches of the RDB." Now, did you understand the difference between the staff and the expanded staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staff operated with some dozen people, that was the actual staff. It is a fact that the decision says that chiefs of secretariats of the interior and heads of the sectors and departments who functioned as members of the secretariat in the same city comprised the expanded staff. That's what it says. But I don't remember that a single meeting was held with an expanded staff. We had meetings with senior officers, usually when people would come from Belgrade, either the assistant minister Obrad Stevanovic or the minister. So these people did not take part in the work of the staff just as Trajkovic, Lukovic, and Gajic didn't. The decision says one thing, but that's not how it functioned in reality. We said that General Lukic couldn't and nobody from the public security sector could supervise the work of somebody from the state security sector and vice versa. So chiefs -- he wasn't able to supervise the work of the chiefs of the State Security Service, sector, or its departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But the minister can delegate task or work to members of both the RDB and the RJB, right? He has authority over both?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you what happened in practice. For as long as the public security sector existed --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you. You're not answering my question. Doesn't the minister have authority over both the RDB and the RJB? He does, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time he did but no longer now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But in the summer of 1998 there was a serious problem in Kosovo that the MUP was trying to deal with in terms of the terrorism, and doesn't it make sense for the minister to create a staff that includes people from both the RDB and the RJB to try and deal with this? Because the minister can't come down to Kosovo every day to try to deal with these problems. So in a sense, this is him delegating and creating this staff to contain members of both the RJB and the RDB to try and deal with the problem. Isn't that why this staff has people from both the DB and the JB? That makes sense, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's precisely what the minister did, but the staff did not function in that composition from July onwards, not in that composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't know if you have the document in front of you, but under item number 2 it said: "The staff is tasked with planning, organizing, and managing the activities and use of the organizational units of the ministry, both the sent and attached units." Can you explain to me what the sent and attached units are? Who are they? What are they in June/July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you repeat which paragraph? I didn't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's paragraph number 2. Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman II on page 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's not Roman numerical in my English, but it may be. I'm sorry, we're looking for P1505. You may have the wrong one on the screen. I can hand you the hard copy, Colonel, if that will assist. Do you find it? It's right below that passage of other members of the ministry may be appointed on request of the head?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. First of all, can you explain to me what the sent and attached units refers to.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I know what the sent units are. As for the attached, I really don't know because they were secretariats with their personnel. Now, the units that were attached, I really don't know unless this refers to something that I'm not familiar with. And they are being sent down there to suppress terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the answer I read in English was you said: "I know what the sent units are." Can you tell us who they are?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the PJP detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what about JSO?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: JSO is a unit of the state security sector, one unit of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that. Is that an organizational unit of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is the SAJ an organizational unit of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. SAJ comes within public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. But it is an organizational unit of the ministry, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what about the PJP, are the PJP --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: PJP is a unit on the basis of gathering, the difference being that special anti-terrorist unit has its permanent composition. As for PJP, it is established ad hoc, which is to say when a minister or a person authorised by a minister issues a decision for them to be established, assembled, and sent to perform a task. PJP is composed out of secretariat of the interior who have territorial competency, that is to say regular police force. When they are not engaged in carrying out regular tasks and obligations, members of PJP units carry out their regular police tasks within their own secretariats. Somebody is a head of a patrol, somebody is a head of a sector, a chief of a police station, and something like that. So they go back to their regular jobs when they are not engaged in PJPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When they are engaged in PJP, is the PJP a PJP detachment, is that considered an organizational unit of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to be quite specific, but it seems to me that in the decision on establishing this decision this is set forth. I can't claim this with full certainty because I haven't seen such decisions for a while, but I think that they are considered an organizational unit when they are carrying out their PJP tasks, when they are being mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the staff task is to plan, organize, and manage the activities and use of those units. And below that it says: "Also the staff is tasked with planning, organizing, directing, and coordinating the activities of the organizational units of the ministry in carrying out complex security operations." And these joint operations with the VJ against the KLA, these anti-terrorist actions, would you not classify those as complex security operations?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, please allow me to make a correction. As far as I can remember now, speaking of organizational units, I think that PJPs are not organizational units, but I think they are commanders -- once a unit is established or assembled, I think its commander has a status of an authorised officer. I think that it is not considered on organizational unit within the ministry structure. Because when you see an organogramme of the ministry, there are no PJPs there, they are not considered organizational units, but their commanders do have a status of a senior officer. If I remember the decision well. Now, would you please repeat your question since I gave more thought to this other issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I suggest that we take our break now and I will ask the question after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Hannis. We shall do that. A break again, Mr. Mijatovic, for half an hour. Could you again please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you again at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Colonel, the question I wanted to ask you before we took the break was whether or not you would agree with me that these joint actions that the MUP and the VJ took against the KLA in late July 1998 through the end of September 1998, would you not classify those as "complex security operations," in that they oftentimes involved several units from both the VJ and the MUP and sometimes hundreds of men and large, heavy weapons? Doesn't that qualify as complex security action?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it does, but the paragraph states that it was planned for the staff to plan and lead the work of the border units of the ministry but not the VJ, that's what it means, and this was about police activity alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, but it also talks about coordinating the use of those units, and that's exactly what General Lukic was doing when he went to those Joint Command meetings, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the general did at those meetings, but this is -- I mean, it was planned that he should lead and organize the work, but only of the units of the ministry and not the army as well. Because involved in these anti-terrorist activities were both the army units and the police units jointly, but not in these complex security tasks because these were carried out by units of the Ministry of the Interior alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that the MUP staff had no role in that, in coordinating that activity, in planning or organizing or directing those organizational units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The staff was not planning, organizing, or directing organizational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija. They did that themselves because, as I've been saying, the staff did not have those powers since the plan to combat terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija had been adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, if I understand what you have been saying for the last few days, you're saying that the MUP staff didn't do any of those things it was tasked to do in this exhibit from the 16th of June, 1998; is that right, it did none of those things?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm talking about the plan, when the plan was adopted this solution was revoked. When the plan to combat terrorism was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where does it say it was revoked? There's still a necessity to coordinate activities with the VJ, and isn't that what MUP staff was supposed to do? Or are you saying that was left entirely to the low-level units on the ground to kind of do for themselves. Is that what you're trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I was talking about was the method, the working method, based on this global plan or basic plan there are a number of different names that are used. I didn't see it, I don't know what exactly the name was. It was based on this that the Pristina Corps produced documents based on which they acted, and these documents were forwarded to units because they were in reference to those units. And the police units that were involved in these tasks and the VJ units that were involved in these tasks on the ground were coordinating these activities and acting on them. The staff did not produce those plans, did not organize or run these activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I don't know if I have misunderstood this, but if you look at the answer at line 7 on page 74, the witness makes a distinction between anti-terrorist activities and complex security tasks, and there are these two separate sections to paragraph 2 of the decision. And your question was suggesting that the joint actions of the VJ and the MUP were complex security operations. And I take it you haven't missed the distinction the witness is making in distinguishing between those which were entirely MUP tasks, he says, and the anti-terrorist or suppression of terrorism activity which was joint activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I understood him earlier to be making a distinction, but as I understood his evidence basically the independent actions taken by the MUP were really small-scale actions. I thought that's what he said in his testimony or his answers to Mr. Cepic. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I will ask a question --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- hopefully will clarify this. Mr. Mijatovic, you have been recorded in English as saying: "In these complex security tasks, these were carried out by units of the Ministry of the Interior alone." Now, is that an accurate translation of what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's in reference to pure police tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, can you describe for me or give me an example of a complex security task?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A complex security task for the secretariat would be this, for example, a small-scale anti-terrorist action which it pursues according to its own plan. That's what we talked about when we talked about combatting terrorism. This wasn't just about combat, it was about other activities too, and eventually there might be a need for some small-scale anti--terrorist operation, a low-intensity one but for the secretariat this is a complex security task because it is outside of what is normally considered its purview or its regular tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You may or may not understand my difficulty in comprehending that distinction, that something simple should be described officially as complex.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure how I should put this. Regular business is no problem for the secretariat but if, for example, say a group of dangerous criminals must be arrested and what this calls for is the involvement of two secretariats, then coordination between the two secretariats is also called for, this calls for more people, and this is a complex security task, but the army is not involved in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me try to be more specific then. Can you actually give an example that you remember taking place in fact? And try to ignore the comments that may be coming from your left and answer it from your own recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't recollect a single task where this was required and where the staff needed to plan something like this. I really don't remember a single one. I don't even recollect that the staff ever organized such an action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your preparation for testifying here, you did see some of those Joint Command orders from March and April of 1999, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you saw the size and complexity of those actions, did you not, that they involved sometimes elements of multiple VJ brigades, PJP, sometimes even PJP, JSO, and the SAJ, hundreds if not thousands of men. Wouldn't you say that those were complex security actions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that was done based on that plan that we talked about, the plan from 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the plan didn't work itself. It needed people to make it happen and it must have needed somebody from the MUP to be involved in making it happen, or are you saying it was entirely done by the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You can tell by looking at it that there were police units and VJ units, but it was done at a local level, as far as I remember. And the order that you were showing me, those orders were something that was done by the army and the police too were involved. They weren't large-scale actions, but these were carried out wherever required as part of combatting terrorism and as part of this basic plan because the plan said that the VJ and the police would be carrying out such activities together.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you not see that some of those actions involved territories covering a geographical area that involved more than one SUP, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we're talking about the activities of the army and the police, meaning this paragraph 2 in item 2 -- what I'm saying is this. If the police were to do this alone, that's what this is about, it's about police business, what the police do on their own, now I'm talking about the first paragraph from II, whenever the army and the police worked together this would always be based on the plan that had been adopted sometime early in July in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, but who from the MUP helped make that plan work? There must have been some personnel from the MUP to help make that plan from July 1998 work. How would the VJ know which units from the MUP were available? Didn't that take some coordination with somebody in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I spoke about that too over the course of my testimony. The plan was adopted and the minister with his associates was there. This meant that the plan was adopted and was to be acted upon, was to be put into practice. After that, the assistant minister, General Stevanovic, came and the sector chief, General Djordjevic, and there was this meeting with the officers where General Djordjevic informed the police leaders in Kosovo and Metohija that such and such a plan had been adopted and that the police units would now be joining those activities. In practical terms, that was his approval and also his order for the units to start launching anti-terrorist activities together with members of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I think I recall you do -- you did say something about this yesterday, but I'm not sure you answered the question I'm trying to get at. At page 22326 when Mr. Cepic was asking you some questions, I believe, you mentioned: "Adamovic was in charge of operational affairs, he participated in providing information, or rather, he provided information for the planning of anti-terrorist activities to the Pristina Corps. He knew where the units were, he followed that, he followed the problems they had, and so on and so forth." So is not Adamovic, a member of the staff, one of the persons who was coordinating complex security actions with the VJ pursuant to the plan that you have been talking about, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is something that was done by Lieutenant-Colonel Dusko Adamovic. He provided an information for each and every action that was to be planned by the Pristina Corps. He would call them, he would see what units could be involved, and then Dusko Adamovic provided that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Fila on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm afraid we're not headed in the right direction. On the screen we see a MUP document and there is not a shred of the army's presence there. This is about police, and I think he's explained about five times already, these are complex security tasks but of the MUP, of the police. And then the Prosecutor is reading this back to him in order to link this up with the army. If he's asking him about the joint actions taken by the MUP and the army, then this is not the document that we should be using. We should put this document away, but he's explained this at least ten times so far both to you, Your Honours, and to the Prosecutor, that this no longer applied once the plan in Belgrade had been adopted. That's what he's saying. It's for you to judge, but now this is being read back to him, complex security tasks, and when this is something that we apply to the army the least we can say is that it is beyond measure, it's immoderate. And when he's explaining about complex security tasks when the MUP has a large-scale action, the MUP, the MUP alone, is arresting a group of terrorists, that's what he's talking about, that's what he's trying to explain. So I'm afraid that we're talking at cross-purposes here, and I don't think this will end well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The problem with that objection I think is that even confining the second part of paragraph 2 to MUP activities that do not involve the VJ at all, the witness says that the MUP staff had nothing to do with these. It still didn't plan, organize, direct, or coordinate these activities; they were entirely for the local SUPs to deal with. So the controversy is a wider one than simply whether the VJ were involved or not. I understand your concern because the questioning is repetitive, but it is a difficult area, and we may be assisted by it. It may be appropriate to observe that certainly if the -- as long as the -- the translation is entirely accurate, one difference between these two -- one other difference between these two parts of paragraph 2 is that the second part seems to be confined to regular units within Kosovo, whereas the first one seems to contemplate units that are not in Kosovo but come into Kosovo. However, I and my colleagues appreciate your difficulty, Mr. Hannis, in trying to fully understand this and we will not disallow the approach that you're taking. We will allow you to continue with this line so far as you think it will be helpful to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I'll try. And for my learned friend across the way, I promise I'll try and put up the Joint Command notes before I'm finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, you mentioned that Adamovic was the one who had this duty, and you were asked further: "How does he decide which detachment is supposed to take part in this action?" And your answer at page 22328 was: "Well, he's not the one who decides. He's the one who provides information what units are there in the area and which units can be used." My question about that is: If Adamovic doesn't decide which MUP units will be used, who does? Does he just provide a list of names of units that are in the area and available to the VJ, and then the VJ says, I'll take number 1, and number 3, and number 5? How did that work?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I was saying is this: Depending on the area in which an anti-terrorist activity was being carried out, he provided information as to which MUP units were in the area so that they might be reckoned with and become part of the plan. There was no need to take any decisions - just by way of an example. The 37th Detachment, if they happened to be in the area where an army brigade was supposed to carry out some activities with them, it was logical that it should carry out these activities and not that another unit was brought from another area. That was my explanation. There was no special need to have any decisions because the unit was there, was in the area, and that unit would now be involved. Because the decision had been taken for units to get involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, but I guess maybe, in fairness to you, I haven't clearly understood this. Did it work then that the VJ first told Adamovic, I need 300 men; and then Adamovic said, These 300 are available. Is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. They didn't say later on it has to be this or that detachment, but they said Dusko Adamovic says we have this or that unit in the area that can get involved and they go on in planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Several times you've answered questions by saying in principle, yes; but I want to know in reality, is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So he first got the information from the VJ about how many men they needed, and then he said which units were available; and then the VJ incorporated those units into the plan. Am I still following you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do they tell him how many men are needed, I don't know. They ask which unit can get involved, and then Dusko says this unit is in the area, therefore that unit can get involved, you can expect that unit to get involved. Whether manpower was discussed or not, that is not something I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you agreed with Mr. Hannis that Adamovic says, We have this or that unit in the area that can get involved and they go on in planning. Now, once the units to be involved are identified, who goes on with the planning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The planning is done by the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If, for example, the VJ needed 200 men and Adamovic knew he had 600 available in the area, would he not be the one who would decide which 200 he was going to say to the army were available or would he advise them of all 600, say, from three different units and let the army choose or do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the details, how they went about this. I wasn't involved. Probably Dusko Adamovic would be better-placed to explain that. These are details I was not familiar with and there was no need for me to be familiar with this because this was something Dusko was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As a general principle would you agree with me that in a hypothetical situation like that, that the MUP would be in a better position to know which ones were best choices. For example, Adamovic would know better out of those three groups of 200 each which ones were rested, which ones were more experienced, which ones had just finished being involved in another action, et cetera, right? He would know better than VJ about that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as police units were concerned, certainly he knew better; how, I don't know, I can't discuss that, I can't discuss any details. How did he know that. Did he keep his own records, did he talk to the detachment commanders as to who could be involved, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mentioned in connection with some of these joint actions with the VJ that the extracts of the maps were sent by the Pristina Corps. Now, who were they sent to in the MUP? Did it go to the MUP staff or to a particular individual? You may have told us that yesterday, but I missed it in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map extracts for anti-terrorist activities in which the VJ and the police were involved jointly were something that normally arrived at the staff, and the staff would send it along to whichever units were involved in these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. We saw in some instances that the JSO and the SAJ were engaged in some of the joint actions. Who forwarded those excerpts to the JSO? Was that you or somebody else on the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I remember. It certainly wasn't me, but the same principle was applied as far as I know. They would receive maps at the staff -- maps arrived for them at the staff, and then this would be forwarded along with the units of the public security, depending on where the unit was, and then a courier would be there or someone from the PJP and he would be given these documents so that he might bring it to them since he was passing by the staff, so the same route, in one word.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Same answer for the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless SAJ commander sent his own courier or came by himself. I think it was done on the same principle. It's possible that he came on his own personally, but Dusko Adamovic would be best placed to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the answer in relation to the JSO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have said, as far as I remember the maps were sent to the staff and then a courier from the unit from the public security who went there for the purposes or for the needs of his own unit would carry this. This was just a courier service. They would do a favour to us, as far as I can remember. But Dusko Adamovic would be better placed to tell you that because he was directly involved in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So isn't that an example of at least Dusko Adamovic on the staff coordinating these activities? Because he's at least passing on the orders received from the VJ and making sure they get to the appropriate organizational units, the JSO or the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Cepic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, I understood the witness to say that it was just excerpts from the maps of the Army of Yugoslavia, not orders, as Mr. Hannis is quoting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, after the war started it was orders -- sorry, after the resubordination order it was orders; until then, it was only maps. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct. I think I may have started out talking about the maps, but I'm talking about throughout 1998 and 1999 whether it was just maps or whether it was both maps and orders. Wouldn't you agree with me that by doing that Mr. Adamovic, for the staff, is helping coordinate?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have said, Adamovic was the one who provided information and forwarded documents to the units. If this is what you mean by coordination, then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did Adamovic include anything else when he forwarded the maps and later on after late April the orders? Did he include anything else with those that came from the MUP staff? For example, a note enclosed, Please find the map and the order from the VJ for action next Tuesday? Or did he simply forward what he received from the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would simply forward to the police units taking part in these activities whatever he had received from the Army of Yugoslavia. So the staff did not produce any additional documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: For some of the other questions about this you told me Mr. Adamovic would be the best one to ask about it. How is it that you know that he did not include anything else with the maps and the orders?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he didn't because he wasn't able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what he could have included. He didn't plan, he didn't write any orders, he didn't draw any maps, he didn't do anything additionally. I know that much. I apologise. He could have sent out some other mail, for example, a document that was forwarded to the secretariats or unit commanders on a different matter. But as for some particular action, when it comes to maps or orders, no, there was nothing additional there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I want to ask you now about some of the meetings that we have documents for, and the first one I'd like you to look at is Exhibit Number P2805, which is regarding a meeting on the 11th of -- I'm sorry, on the 5th of November, 1998. I can give you a hard copy, Colonel. And let's have look at page 2 in both the English, and I guess it's page 3 in the B/C/S. You see that the cover page for the minutes of the meeting held on 5 November 1998 starting at 1415 hours. Do you find that, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I see your name in the list of people attending. The first name we see is President Milutinovic and then the Minister Stojiljkovic, General Djordjevic and Markovic and Sreten Lukic. Some of the civilians that we've heard associated with the Joint Command, Mr. Sainovic, Mr. Minic, Mr. Andjelkovic, Mr. Matkovic, General Pavkovic, and so on, including 13 representatives of the Pristina Corps. Do you remember attending this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see that Mr. -- or General Lukic presided over the meeting and then turned the floor over to President Milutinovic, who spoke. On that page can you see where President Milutinovic starts speaking? Now we're on page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Your page is different from ours. Can you go about to the seventh line down right after the reference to an announcement by the Republic of Serbia on the 27th of October. He's talking about that agreement between Holbrooke and Milosevic, and you see it says: "He added that on 29 October 1998 a meeting with the president," Milosevic that would be, "was held regarding the situation within the army and the police." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He also said that on the 29th of October, is that what you mean? Yes, I've found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall him mentioning that meeting on the 29th of October or that meeting between the army and the police and President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what? I see this stated in the minutes, but if you expect me to remember who said all those years ago, I wouldn't be able to do that. It is stated in the minutes that he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. If you could go further on, I think you have to go to the next page, and it's about the next page of the B/C/S and it's about four or five lines down from the top.
