On English we need to go to the bottom of -- about two-thirds of the way down on page 3. Are you there, Colonel? One of the things that Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. If that sentence begins with: "For the Army of Yugoslavia ..." If that's what you had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. My translation here reads: "Everything remains the same for the Yugoslav Army and police Joint Command. VJ units are not withdrawing and police forces are only reduced only by the part that has already been withdrawn ..." Do you see that reference to Joint Command by President Milutinovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that doesn't refresh your memory about hearing the term Joint Command used in 1998 in your presence?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I have said, I can't remember every word that somebody uttered, and I told you that I had heard of that term before President Milutinovic came to Kosovo and Metohija. But for me that simply meant nothing special because I wasn't aware of the existence of that command, I never felt its presence, its existence. I didn't see tasks issued by it. I simply didn't feel that it existed in any way, and I have already said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could have up now Exhibit P2166 again, please. I'll trade you, Colonel, and give you a hard copy of this. You saw that document while preparing for your testimony, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is that Inter-departmental Staff meeting that I think I even mentioned with you earlier. Without going through the pages I will tell you that Mr. Milosevic at page 1; General Pavkovic at page 1 of your B/C/S, page 2 of the English; General Lukic, page 7, English, page 8 of the B/C/S; Mr. Minic page 9, English, page 10, B/C/S; General Perisic page 12 of both English and B/C/S; President Milutinovic at page 12 of both; and Mr. Sainovic at page 13 of both English and B/C/S refer specifically to the Joint Command. And all these guys are talking about the Joint Command. It's mentioned at that meeting you attended. General Lukic was going to Joint Command meetings and you tell us you didn't really feel the presence of any such body. Is that still your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I still stand by that. I reiterate, the MUP staff was never given any single task by that Joint Command nor was any member of the Ministry of the Interior in that situation. None of them ever received any task with a heading Joint Command nor did they orally receive a task from some Joint Command nor was there any obligation to inform some Joint Command --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How can you say that when you don't know about the Joint Command? Do you know that General Stevanovic and General Djordjevic also attended Joint Command meetings in 1998? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that in addition to General Lukic they participated in those meetings, but I wasn't aware, I didn't know that those were meetings of the Joint Command. Nothing indicated that, nor did I ever hear from them, We are going to a meeting of the Joint Command. Nor did they, upon their return, say, At the Joint Command we were told that we have such and such task. And as for what is stated here in these minutes, as I have told you, yes, I have heard of this term being used, but I never felt this Joint Command, I didn't know that it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I stopped you, though, because you were going on and saying nobody from the MUP ever got a task from the Joint Command. If you don't know about the meetings, you don't know who attended, you don't know what was said there, you can't say that, can you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what was discussed in those meetings. I know and I saw in these notes that Obrad Stevanovic and Djordjevic and military generals and people from the politics attended these meetings. But as I have said, I didn't know that those were meetings of the Joint Command because I never heard anybody say, I'm going to a meeting of the Joint Command. No. They normally went to meetings of various structures that coordinated these activities. That's why I'm saying that I was never aware that that was Joint Command. And I do not deny that in the notes ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you finish?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I do not deny that in the notes that I have seen, in the heading it says ZK for Joint Command, but I wasn't aware that they went to the meetings of the Joint Command. I simply didn't know that it existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You saw Exhibit P1468, the notes of meetings of the Joint Command between 22nd July 1998 and the end of October 1998? Did you see that document in preparing for your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it, and I have it here. I just didn't read all of that. I just took a brief look because I simply had no time to read all of this and I can't really tell you that I am aware of every document and its contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. I don't expect you to know everything that was in those notes. I will tell you that my rough count of the meetings recorded there, there are either 69 or 70 meetings between the 22nd of July and 30th of October, according to that document; and it appears that at least at 58 of those meetings, General Lukic was in attendance. You didn't know that? You didn't know he was going to these meetings every other day or so?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that he did not attend those meetings. I don't know how many there were in total. I know that there were meetings between representatives of various state organs, that is to say police, army, and people from various state structures, politics, state security, and so on. I know that those meetings were held, but I don't know that it was called Joint Command, that it represented Joint Command. To me it resembled coordination. I attended a meeting where people briefed on whatever they had to say and there were no conclusions or tasks emanating from that; simply, everybody did what they had to do, and it wasn't my impression, it wasn't my impression that this was Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware that General Lukic participated in a recorded interview with the OTP prior to the beginning of this case?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Kosovo and Metohija with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Frankly, I'm not even sure of the location. I think it was. It was after the war. Have you seen the transcript of his interview with the OTP in preparing for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Since we previously talked about the meetings of the Joint Command and then you linked this with the interview with the OTP, I simply thought that it referred to something that took place in Kosovo and Metohija. I apologise. My misunderstanding. During the proofing I partially looked over that statement. I didn't have time to read everything, but I saw it partially, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you see enough -- and for the record that's Exhibit P948. Did you have occasion to see enough of it to see that he told the OTP investigators that he was attending Joint Command meetings in 1998 and in 1999? Did you read enough of it to see that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that I have read somewhere that he said the so-called Joint Command. I'm not sure, but I don't know about him being adamant that there was a Joint Command. Let me reiterate that I didn't know that Joint Command existed, nor did he ever at the time say to me that he was going to a meeting of the Joint Command or that we had received a task from the Joint Command. So there was no way for me to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to save time I would indicate for the record that there are references to this matter at pages 48 to 50, 84 to 85, 97 to 105, 109 to 113, 120 to 122, 146 to 148, and 160 to 163.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So even having seen that to the extent that you did, that doesn't change your opinion about whether or not there was a body that existed in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and/or in 1999 that was called the Joint Command, regardless of what its competencies were? Just talk about the name of it, are you still saying there wasn't any such body?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position is that I do not know that this body existed. Now, as to why somebody called it this, I don't know. It's not clear to me. Let me repeat that I have never at the staff seen an order or a task received from the Joint Command nor did we ever receive any of their reports on any issues, at least I'm not aware of that. This is why I'm saying that I never felt its existence. They didn't have offices, they didn't have telephones, they didn't have anything that would indicate to me that there existed such a thing as a Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You didn't see a document showing that they had a radio call-sign or code-name?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You would agree with me, however, that General Lukic is in a better position than you to know whether or not there was a Joint Command in existence and meeting in Kosovo in 1998 and/or in 1999, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew what type of meetings he attended. I don't know whether he understood that it was a Joint Command at the time or not; that's up to him. But I know that he never told us about any Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. You saw from those notes that there was one meeting that you were present for even though you tell us at the time you weren't aware it was a Joint Command meeting, right? You talked about that earlier with Mr. Branko Lukic, the lawyer for General Lukic. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the meeting, yes, and you can see that in the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I could hand you that page, it's page 141 of the B/C/S and page 157 in the English of Exhibit P1468. I just want to try and clear up something in connection with that. You mentioned in that meeting about a five-man monitoring group arriving from Finland today to investigate the situation in Kosovo and Metohija and to exhume bodies. And I think when you answered a question about that before you mentioned Racak because you were aware that there was some Finnish forensic team involved with that, but you know Racak was in January of 1999 so that cannot be what you're referring to here, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I remember that after Racak experts came in in relation to this event, and I saw in the minutes, but I can't remember, that this team came. I can't deny that this team came. I can't remember that though, and I can see in the minutes that their arrival was reported, but I can't remember that they came and why they came. But obviously I wouldn't report about their arrival if they had not arrived. I just simply can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me quickly show you one other document. This is 6D197. This is a MUP dispatch dated the 12th of October, 1998. Have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that. No, no, what I have is 10th of December. I don't know if it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's also 10th December on the screen, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you -- had you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware of an incident involving an alleged massacre of civilians in Gornje Obrinje around the end of September 1998? That was a high-profile incident that got a lot of media attention. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I read in some document while I was proofed about corpses in a number of locations, and if I remember well Gornje Obrinje was mentioned. In certain locations investigations were conducted, but as far as I remember, it wasn't possible to do that in Obrinje due to security reasons because there were a lot of members of the so-called KLA there. The area around had been mined, and if I remember well, one MUP vehicle had driven over a mine and five policemen were killed. I'm not sure, but I think this pertains to Gornje Obrinje and this information came in from the media about there being corpses and so on and the SUP wanted to go and do whatever needed to be done, but they just simply couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This sounds like a lengthy business or are you going to deal with it quite quickly?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I think I'm going to break here, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. -- Have you a way to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if I can organize I can be done in an hour and a half tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Back tomorrow again then, Mr. Mijatovic. Could you now please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we will see you again at 9.00 tomorrow morning in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [The witness stands down].
